findings.discovery: Fuel-rate PID 015E is the preferred path when announced and returning a valid parsed value. It is ECU-reported, not an independent fuel-flow-meter measurement.
findings.decision: Keep 015E first; never downgrade a valid 015E reading to MAF/MAP in the same sample.

findings.discovery: Fuel volume can be estimated from air mass flow, stoichiometric air/fuel ratio and fuel density; the result changes materially with fuel type and mixture.
findings.decision: Use MAF only after the 0110 PID is advertised and its individual response passes parsing and plausibility gates. Mark the result as estimated.

findings.discovery: MAP + IAT + RPM + engine displacement can derive an approximate air mass flow through the ideal gas law; volumetric efficiency is an uncertain engine-specific parameter.
findings.decision: Keep MAP as the second fallback, label as estimated and preserve VE as a JSON parameter until real Meriva logs and refuelling data can calibrate it.

findings.discovery: The ANP reported a temporary E32 blend for regular gasoline C, effective from 2026-08-01 for 180 days; the common E30 baseline is not current on the research date.
findings.decision: Use E32 as the explicitly dated default when the user selects GASOLINA, mark values as model estimates, and schedule a parameter review by 2027-01-27.

findings.discovery: Hydrous ethanol is not identical to anhydrous/pure ethanol; water fraction changes density and stoichiometric AFR.
findings.decision: Use 95 vol% ethanol plus 5 vol% water literature properties as a provisional proxy, not an exact specification for the user's fuel batch.

findings.discovery: Without PID 0152, the ECU does not reveal the fuel ethanol share; an automatic midpoint is not a measurement and may be wrong for a tank filled with only ethanol or gasoline.
findings.decision: Keep reference E50 only as a visible fallback, encode the percentage in JSON, and advise selecting the actual tank fuel. Never call the result measured.

findings.discovery: The repository's vehicle-specific evidence list marks only 010C as confirmed from a RAW_ECU response; 015E, 0110, 010B, 010F and 0152 remain candidates until verified on the actual adapter/ECU.
findings.decision: Do not claim the new hierarchy is physically validated on the Meriva until RAW_ECU responses and their support bitmap are recorded.

findings.discovery: Open-source OBD guidance describes using tank refill data to calibrate MAP-derived volumetric efficiency; a full-to-full comparison also provides a practical flow correction factor.
findings.decision: Require at least three valid full-to-full intervals before accepting a correction factor; reject factors outside 0.70–1.30 and smooth accepted updates.

knownLimitations: No complete RAW_ECU evidence set (raw responses plus support bitmap) has been recorded for the candidate fuel PIDs on the actual Meriva; physical support and compatibility remain unconfirmed.
PID 0152 interpretation and availability are not confirmed for this KWP/K-Line ECU, especially with Brazilian retail gasoline blend rules.
The MAF formula currently assumes stoichiometric operation unless the model is extended with a valid lambda/equivalence-ratio correction.
The MAP path uses provisional volumetric efficiency 0.80; this is not a calibrated Chevrolet Meriva constant.
Runtime entry and persistence of full-to-full refuelling calibration still require a settings flow and are not implemented by this change.
nextActions: Record RAW_ECU + bitmap evidence for 015E, 0110, 010B, 010F and 0152.
Run the same route while logging speed, MAF or MAP/IAT/RPM and calculated fuel rate.
Compare at least three full-to-full fuel-up intervals against integrated estimated litres.
Before 2027-01-27, review the temporary E32 parameter against current ANP policy.
Only add lambda/fuel-trim corrections after confirming supported PID semantics and actual response quality.
